chapter: Metronome, Billie Holiday, Cleveland and Atlantic
title: The Metronome All-Star date of 1946
summary: He was surprised to be chosen, was classed as miscellaneous instrument in polls, and describes the atmosphere and RCA recording.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Do you remember much about the Metronome All-star date you did in 1946?
A little bit about it, yeah. I was picked -- I was surprised that I was picked because I never won anything, you know -- Down Beat... I think I came in second once...
You were talking about the Down beat poll -- how did they usually categorize you?

Miscellaneous instrument. I wasn't compared to the great guys -- although I was playin' with 'em, you know. So somehow or other I think I made second in Down beat, and I won the Metronome. That was with a lot of Duke Ellington's men. I had a picture -- there was quite a few fellas on there
Harry Edison reads personnel -- Tiny Grimes and Billy Bauer on guitar. Do you remember Bauer being there also?
No, I don't even know Billy Barrel... No
Was that an enjoyable recording session for you?

Oh yeah, sure. Very much. To be playing with that type of person with a 'miscellaneous' instrument for sure. It couldn't be beat with that clientele, man. Those guys -- the greatest. Yeah, I was happy to be there. I didn't have a chance to play nothin' much...
Nice, them guys, they always tellin' jokes and things -- no static. No who's who + what's what. Just name somethin', they go ahead and play it.
Do you remember where it was?
Do you remember the recording studio at all? The equipment -- anything unusual about it
I really don't know. The only studio I can remember, I don't know if they recorded there was Nola studios, but I don't think it was there. What company did it?

Well it had to be one of their studios, then.

I know they didn't have tracks and things like that. If you made a mistake at the end, you had to play the whole thing over again. They couldn't patch it up. And probably about two mikes, you know. So, that's funny how those guys made all those good records back there and they didn't have all this buttons and things they got these days. And one microphone maybe two for the whole band, and shit, they came out great. Now they got all this equipment that they -- well I guess it saves time, you can patch up somethin'. Or record one person one day and the next time if they can't get together, and then mix it together.
